column1: # Which Blacksmith tier makes a forge recipe (the forge, the anvil, the Skyforge, the Dawnguard forge).
# Nate, 2026-09-30: "keep the approved ladder". The tiers are skills.json blacksmith.tiers, which players read today
# ("Tiers decide which metals you may work"), and the ladder in BLACKSMITH_TIERS_PROPOSAL.md:
#   1 Iron, hide, fur, leather   2 Steel, silver, dwarven, elven, chainmail, mithril   3 Orcish, steel plate, scaled,
#   Nordic   4 Ebony, glass, stalhrim   5 Dragonbone, dragonscale, Daedric
# A recipe's tier comes from, in order:
#   1. edid     the result's editor id matches the pattern (* wildcard, case-insensitive; first match wins). Needed where
#               a material has no keyword of its own: Beyond Skyrim's chainmail carries ArmorMaterialIron/Steel.
#   2. keyword  the result's material keywords; the highest tier among them (a Dragonplate-based variant is Dragon).
#   3. perk     the vanilla smithing perk(s) the recipe asks for today; the highest. Only for results whose keywords
#               are not listed below (Immersive Armors' faction sets, More Craftable Equipment, WAF, guild armour).
#   4. default  and the row is marked "review" in forge_tiers.csv.
# The manual column (Nate, 2026-09-30, "do both, gives scholars more meaning"): a recipe of that material also needs its
# smithing manual read (HasSpell DBO_Manual_<manual>), whatever the tier; manuals.tsv lists them. Empty = no manual:
# tier 1 metals, jewellery, and regalia made from a Dragon Priest's mask. A recipe takes the manual of the rule that
# gave its tier (for a keyword tier, the manual of its highest-tier keyword).
# make_tables.py applies this and writes forge_tiers.csv, whose tier and manual columns Nate may change per recipe.
